summary: Read an integer inside the closed span from 1 to 3999 and write it with Roman symbols. The basic symbols and their weights are I for 1, V for 5, X for 10, L for 50, C for 100, D for 500, and M for 1000. Normally place heavier weights to the left of lighter ones. Exactly six subtractive layouts are legal: I standing ahead of V or X means 4 or 9, X standing ahead of L or C means 40 or 90, and C standing ahead of D or M means 400 or 900. In every other case, do not put a lighter symbol ahead of a heavier one.
notes: Compare after trimming trailing newlines. The input is tokens in the same order as the method parameters.
